{{Quote|One thing ties them together&mdash;credits. The pursuit of lucre motivates every species that recognizes a monetary system.|Feltipern Trevagg|audio=Credits.flac|<ref name="Nightlily">[[Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale (audio drama)|"Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale" audio drama]]</ref>}}
The '''Galactic Credit Standard''',{{Fact}} also called '''Credits Standard''',<ref name="Han Solo's Revenge">''[[Han Solo's Revenge]]''</ref> simply called a '''credit'''<ref name="ANH novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> or '''cred''', colloquially referred to as '''Republic Dataries''', and later known as the '''Imperial Credit''', was the main [[Currency/Legends|currency]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] since the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

The Galactic Credit Standard was established on [[Sojourn (moon)|Sojourn]]. From its inception, the credit was backed by the immense natural resources of the planet [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]]{{Fact}}, which was claimed by the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] (IGBC). During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the IGBC provided loans and financial aid to both sides, as it would do again decades later for the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]].

One tenth of a credit was a [[Decicred/Legends|decicred]].

==Form==
{{Quote|Information is a commodity. It can be traded, sold, and purchased. And in the end, credits are only as valuable as the secrets they can buy.|Darth Bane|<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>}}
[[File:CreditChip.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A [[Credit chip/Legends|credit chip]]]]
The credit was a form of digital currency with [[Coin/Legends|cards]] in circulation. Although they were about the same size, credits sometimes came in different patterns or designs, most likely depending on how much they were worth. Sometime during the height of the Galactic Republic, [[Credit chip/Legends|credit chips]] became popular. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the credit also came in the form of small metallic [[Credit ingot/Legends|ingots]]. There were also [[Credit cube|cubes]] that were presumably similar to chips. Near the end of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] reign, physical currency increased in popularity as denizens of the galaxy awaited resolution to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Many were wary that credit chips could become worthless following the war.

In some places, such as the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], credits could be accessed via a [[debit code]]. Credits could be transferred or withdrawn from an account card. These were usually used by [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] or [[Pazaak/Legends|pazaak]] players. Bounty hunters also received an agreed amount of credits after completing a task or mission.

==Decline==
{{Quote|Republic credits? Republic credits are no good out here. I need something more real.|Watto to Qui-Gon Jinn on Tatooine|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
[[File:1000CreditCoin-SWMonopoly.png|thumb|250px|An [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] credit [[Coin/Legends|coin]]]]
During the Clone Wars, and even before, many of the galaxy's inhabitants were worried about the war's outcome and the effect it would have on the [[galactic economy]]. Because of this, an overwhelming majority of planets outside the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]] and [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] would not accept credits. These planets and regions began minting their own currencies. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] was creating new currencies at a rate of twenty per day, with the [[InterGalactic Currency Exchange System]] managing the currency.<ref name="HNN - Currency Upheavals Deliver Profits to IBC">''{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|business/13314_1.html|Currency Upheavals Deliver Profits to IBC}}''</ref>

[[File:BigPileOfCredits-SWGTCGGH.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A pile of [[Credit chip/Legends|credit chips]]]]
The Empire continued to use the credit, now called the Imperial Credit, as its main currency, and during the reign of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], there were few who would not accept it. Even the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] used it, along with their own [[Alliance Credit]], as it was the most used and easiest-to-use currency in the galaxy. While larger-denomination coins existed, they weren't widely circulated throughout the galaxy.<ref name="SWRPG2">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref>

After the fracturing of the Empire at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], many different currencies came into existence. Though the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] had reclaimed the credit, it was by no means the most accepted monetary unit in the galaxy. Many regions, including the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]], again minted their own currencies. During this time, exchange rates fluctuated wildly, and indeed it was hard at times to find anyone that would exchange one for another. Traders, smugglers, and legitimate freighters dealt in precious metals and commodities as neither the New Republic nor the Imperial Remnant would accept the other's currency.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Credit_bills.jpg|thumb|Various credit bills from ''Monopoly: Star Wars Saga Edition'']]
In supplemental material [[George Lucas]] wrote in [[1977]] for the use of licensees, he described the "Coin of the Galactic Realm" as having two forms: a "credit unit," which is left without a description, and a flat square coin made out of crystal. The crystal coin was not reproducible by anyone other than the Empire.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>

The credit symbol ({{Cr}}) was created for the ''[[Monopoly Star Wars (board game)|Monopoly Star Wars]]'' board game<ref name="Aurebesh Soup">{{WebCite|url=http://www.echostation.com/features/aurebesh.htm|text=Aurebesh Soup: ''Recipe for a Star Wars Font Phenomenon''|author=[[Stephen Crane|Crane, Stephen]]|date=2000-10-21|work=Echo Station|language=English|quote=When Parker Brothers designed the Star Wars Monopoly game, they incorporated the Aurebesh, also. The 1000-credit coin was taken from a design I had done for a West End product proposal, but which we had passed on to Lucasfilm when the product was not approved. The original was a two-credit coin (other coins were designed, as well, but that's a story for another time). The credit bills incorporated the coin front as part of their design, but were designed by Parker Brothers' artists. Sharp-eyed readers may notice that the word 'credit' was misspelled on the coin part of the bill -- I believe this was fixed in later editions of the game. The sample sheet printed on the back of the rulebook was a reproduction of the sample sheet in ''Imperial Entanglements''. Parker Brothers made a contribution to the Aurebesh, too. They created the credits sign.|archivedate=20160520153232}}</ref> and looks like the [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] letter [[Resh/Legends|Resh]] crossed by two lines in the upper left. The credit sign follows the widespread tradition in real life of governments using a letter from the alphabet crossed by one or two lines to denote a currency: Real-world currency symbols following this tradition include those for the [[Wikipedia:Pound sign|British pound sterling]] (£), the [[Wikipedia:Euro sign|European Union euro]] (€), the [[Wikipedia:Dollar Sign|American dollar]] ($), and the [[Wikipedia:Cent (currency)#Symbol|cent]] (¢).
